basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et dixerunt: Venite, faciamus nobis civitatem et turrem, cujus culmen ascendat ad coelum,'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et dixerunt: Venite, faciamus nobis civitatem et turrem, cujus culmen ascendat ad coelum, et celebremus nomen nostrum antequam dividamur in universas terras. Quod ait cujus culmen, non civitatis, sed turris significat, id est, arcis quam in editiore loco altiorem caeteris moenibus facere disponebant. Mirandum sane qua intentione et culmen suae turris ad coelum usque attollere disponant, et se nihilominus in universas terras dividendos esse perhibeant; nisi forte ita se per orbem dividere vanissima ac superbissima mente cogitabant, ut si forte delectaret pertaesos terrenae habitationis, vel certe si aquae diluvii rursum terris ingruerent, per hanc superiora aeris sive coeli spatia peterent.
